title: Broken Object Level Authorization (IDOR) on Shopping Basket
expected_behavior: Return HTTP 403 Forbidden when User B requests a shopping basket owned by User A (UserId 1).
actual_behavior: Returned HTTP 200 OK with complete JSON basket payload containing User A product inventory and order metadata.
impact_explanation: Horizontal authorization flaw allows any authenticated user or attacker to enumerate and view private customer carts, order contents, and personal identifier tokens.
description: The endpoint /rest/basket/{id} returns customer cart details based solely on the URL path ID parameter. Requesting basket ID 1 using User B credentials successfully returned User A's private product inventory and order metadata without proper ownership verification.

title: Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA) on User Administration
expected_behavior: Strictly restrict full customer list access to administrator role with HTTP 403 Forbidden for non-admins.
actual_behavior: Standard authenticated User A successfully retrieved entire user directory including emails, hashed credentials, and role flags.
impact_explanation: Vertical privilege escalation exposing tenant-wide customer accounts, enabling targeted account takeover and offline credential cracking.
description: Administrative endpoint /api/Users fails to enforce RBAC middleware checks before querying the database, allowing any low-privilege role to view all users.

title: Missing Authentication on Security Questions Directory
expected_behavior: Private system endpoints should require a valid authentication token before answering requests.
actual_behavior: Anonymous requests with no Authorization header successfully retrieved all security question definitions and identifiers.
impact_explanation: Allows unauthenticated reconnaissance of password reset workflows and pre-computation of target answer matrices.
description: Endpoint /api/SecurityQuestions completely omits session authentication checks, returning internal security question models to unauthenticated clients.

title: Mass Assignment Vulnerability in Profile Role Modification
expected_behavior: Profile update endpoints must reject or strip restricted administrative parameters such as role or isAdmin.
actual_behavior: Supplying role: 'admin' in the JSON update payload successfully elevated User B to full administrator privileges with HTTP 200 OK.
impact_explanation: Enables standard low-privilege users to self-promote to full administrator access, compromising system integrity and authorization guarantees.
description: Endpoint /api/Users/{id} directly binds user-supplied JSON properties to the persistent database model without field filtering.
